verified_title: DiT4DiT: Jointly Modeling Video Dynamics and Actions for Generalizable Robot Control
problem: Static VLM features can omit fine motion cues; fully denoising future video is expensive and may overspecialize action features to one imagined outcome.
contribution: Jointly train video and action DiTs with distinct generation, feature-extraction and action diffusion times. Condition control on intermediate visual features from a single backbone pass rather than completed future video.
algorithm: Cosmos-Predict2.5-2B and a causal VAE supply hidden features, default layer18. A GR00T-derived action DiT cross-attends to these features and proprioception. Train joint video/action flow losses with frozen VAE/text encoder. Video time is uniform, action time is complement-Beta, and feature time is described as fixed; Algorithm1 instead samples feature time. Inference uses one feature pass plus action denoising; full video generation is optional.
observations: Language embeddings from Cosmos-Reason1, current RGB and proprioception. Physical G1 uses a head-mounted D435i; single-view self-occlusion is acknowledged. A fresh Gaussian future latent remains an input even with a selected feature time, so fixed time alone does not make features deterministic.
actions: 16-step chunks; appendix pads action dimension32 and state dimension64 with masks. Real embodiment has16DoF, while simulated GR1 has29DoF including hands/waist. These are not direct SO101/M3 interfaces.
embodiment_and_data: LIBERO1693 filtered episodes and GR1 tabletop24000 demonstrations across24 tasks. Physical G1 training uses241450 simulated GR1 pretraining episodes followed by1400 real demos,200/task. Benchmark 'from scratch' means no external ACTION data; pretrained Cosmos video weights remain. Configuration lists32 GPUs and100k steps.
experiments: Four LIBERO suites and RoboCasa24tasks with50 rollouts/task=1200. Seven physical tasks have20 independent trials each=140, plus category/object/quantity shifts. Matched Qwen3DiT uses the same action head and pipeline. Layer/denoising/joint-training ablations include representation plots; t-SNE and silhouette scores are not physical outcomes.
baselines: GR00T-N1.5/N1.6, parameter-matched Qwen3DiT and published LIBERO methods. Robot pretraining differs from the authors' simulated prior; several individual RoboCasa tasks favor baselines despite the improved average.

limitations: Fixed feature-time prose conflicts with random time in Algorithm1. 'From scratch' still uses general video pretraining. One egocentric view and absent tactile/force inputs limit contact observability. Temporal feature clusters do not identify contact dynamics. Large backbones and GPU training require separate edge validation.
code_and_license: No pinned implementation, weights, data terms or license files audited; no execution. Cosmos, Qwen and GR00T components have independent terms.
